title: Cyclone Arnab Strengthens: IMD Raises Gusts to 150 Kmph, Landfall Near Yanam on Wednesday
excerpt: The India Meteorological Department upgraded very severe Cyclone Arnab to 125-135 kmph winds gusting to 150 kmph, with landfall expected between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by Wednesday forenoon and dozens of trains cancelled.
body:
• The IMD has upgraded very severe Cyclone Arnab to sustained winds of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph, up from 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph.
  • Landfall is expected by Wednesday forenoon between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, with a storm surge of 1.0 to 2.0 metres forecast near Kakinada and Yanam.
  • Indian Railways has cancelled dozens of trains — The Hindu put the total at 61, up from 53 reported earlier on Tuesday — and schools have shut in vulnerable coastal districts.
  • If you have family in coastal Andhra Pradesh or southern Odisha, check train status before travel on October 28 and follow IMD and state disaster authority advisories only.

Very severe Cyclone Arnab intensified over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to raise its wind forecast as the storm closed on the Andhra Pradesh coast. Satellite pictures on Tuesday morning showed the cyclone had developed a well-defined eye a short distance off the Visakhapatnam coast, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

The IMD located the storm at 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday about 240 km east of Kakinada, 340 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam, 370 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 410 km east of Bapatla, moving north-west at about 20 kmph. It is expected to move west-northwestwards until Tuesday evening and then turn northwestwards to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts.

What has changed in the forecast

"on Tuesday about 240 km east of Kakinada, 340 km east-southeast of Machilipatnam, 370 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 410 km east of Bapatla, moving north-west at about 20 kmph."

The upgrade matters because Arnab is no longer a routine severe storm. The IMD raised maximum sustained winds to 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph, and global models cited by BusinessLine put the probability of the storm intensifying further into an extremely severe cyclone at 100 per cent, up from 83 per cent a day earlier. A separate official note on Tuesday morning put the storm 215 km south-east of Visakhapatnam and warned coastal winds would build from 40-50 kmph on Tuesday morning to 100-110 kmph overnight, according to Nation Press.

The IMD has issued a red warning for Andhra Pradesh, and state authorities have placed all 20 districts on high alert. A storm surge of 1.0 to 2.0 metres is anticipated at landfall, highest near Kakinada and Yanam, and residents have been urged to stay away from the sea, rivers, tanks and structurally weak buildings.

Trains, schools and evacuations

Indian Railways cancelled 53 trains in earlier Tuesday reports, a figure The Hindu's live coverage later put at 61 as the storm approached — travellers should treat any scheduled coastal service on October 28 as at risk and verify status directly with the Railways. Authorities in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha are arranging evacuations, preparing cyclone shelters and deploying disaster response teams, while educational institutions in vulnerable areas have closed, according to News Ei Samay.

The National Crisis Management Committee, chaired by Cabinet Secretary T. V. Somanathan, reviewed preparations on Tuesday. Odisha's Special Relief Commissioner has also warned against spreading misleading information about the cyclone, a sign officials expect rumours to circulate as landfall nears.

What to watch next

Arnab follows days of Videshi coverage of the same system, from its formation in the Bay of Bengal to red alerts in six Odisha districts and the fishing and tourist-entry bans imposed on Monday. The next 24 hours will decide the damage: whether the eye holds its intensity over the shelf waters, how high the surge runs at Kakinada and Yanam, and how much rain falls inland across coastal Andhra, southern Odisha and Bengal, where heavy rain warnings are also in force.

For readers abroad with parents or property on this coast, the actionable steps are narrow and practical: confirm any train or flight before setting out, keep family phone numbers for the state disaster authority handy, and rely on IMD bulletins rather than forwarded videos. Landfall is forecast for Wednesday forenoon — the window for preparation closes on Tuesday night.
